concepts.title: Hot, Cold, and Temperature
concepts.description: Introduction to the sensation of heat, the unreliability of touch for judging heat, and the definition of temperature as a reliable measure.
key_ideas: Sense of touch is not a reliable measure of heat
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of an object
Heat flows from a hotter object to a colder object

concepts.title: Measuring Temperature: Thermometers
concepts.description: Understanding the construction and usage of clinical and laboratory thermometers, including reading scales (Celsius) and safety precautions.
key_ideas: Clinical thermometers measure body temperature (35°C to 42°C)
Laboratory thermometers measure object temperatures (-10°C to 110°C)
Mercury or alcohol expands in the bulb to indicate temperature
Correct method of reading a thermometer level with the eyes

concepts.title: Conductors and Insulators
concepts.description: Classifying materials based on their ability to allow heat to pass through them, distinguishing between good conductors and poor conductors (insulators).
key_ideas: Conductors (e.g., metals like copper, aluminum) allow heat to pass through easily
Insulators (e.g., wood, plastic, air) do not allow heat to pass through easily
Practical uses of insulators in cooking handles and clothing

concepts.title: Sea Breeze and Land Breeze
concepts.description: Explaining the natural phenomena of air movement in coastal areas caused by the differential heating and cooling rates of land and water.
key_ideas: Land heats up and cools down faster than water
Sea Breeze: Cool air moves from sea to land during the day
Land Breeze: Cool air moves from land to sea during the night
This is a natural example of convection currents

concepts.title: Clothing and Heat Absorption
concepts.description: Understanding how surface colors absorb or reflect radiant heat and why specific clothing materials are chosen for different seasons.
key_ideas: Dark surfaces absorb more heat; light surfaces reflect more heat
Woolen clothes keep us warm because wool is an insulator and traps air
Wearing light-colored clothes in summer and dark-colored clothes in winter

concepts.title: Components of Blood
concepts.description: Exploration of the specific cells and fluid that make up human blood, focusing on their distinct functions in the body.
key_ideas: Plasma is the fluid part of blood.
Red Blood Cells (RBC) contain haemoglobin and carry oxygen.
White Blood Cells (WBC) fight against germs and infections.
Platelets are responsible for the clotting of blood.

concepts.title: Blood Vessels: Arteries and Veins
concepts.description: Comparison of the two main types of blood vessels, their structural differences, and the direction in which they carry blood relative to the heart.
key_ideas: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood from the heart to all parts of the body.
Veins carry carbon dioxide-rich blood from all parts of the body back to the heart.
Arteries have thick, elastic walls, while veins have thin walls with valves.
Capillaries are extremely thin tubes connecting arteries to veins.

concepts.title: Human Excretory System
concepts.description: Study of how the human body filters blood to remove waste products, focusing on the organs involved in urine formation and elimination.
key_ideas: The excretory system consists of kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra.
Kidneys filter the blood to remove toxic wastes.
Wastes dissolved in water are removed as urine.
Urine consists of 95% water, 2.5% urea, and 2.5% other waste products.

concepts.title: Transport of Substances in Plants
concepts.description: Introduction to the vascular tissue in plants responsible for moving water, minerals, and food throughout the plant structure.
key_ideas: Plants have pipe-like vessels made of special cells to transport water and nutrients.
Xylem tissue transports water and minerals from roots to the leaves.
Phloem tissue transports food prepared by leaves to other parts of the plant.
Root hairs increase the surface area for absorption of water and minerals.

concepts.title: Transpiration
concepts.description: Analysis of the process of water loss from plant leaves and how this process aids in the upward movement of water.
key_ideas: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves through stomata.
This process generates a suction pull (transpiration pull).
The suction pull helps pull water to great heights in tall trees.
Transpiration also helps in cooling the plant.
